context.label: Prison, death, and public memory

observations.body: Mark adds Herod’s fear and interest, Herodias’s hostility, the banquet guests, the guard’s action, and burial by John’s disciples.
observations.label: Mark expands the account of John’s death

observations.body: The passage presents Hearing, fearing, guarding, demanding, and killing as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Hearing, fearing, guarding, demanding, and killing

payload.posture: Read Mark 6:14–29 as one movement in John the Baptist's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: Herod protects John yet orders his death
payload.title: Mark expands the account of John’s death
